outcome: The conjecture was fully resolved decades before the frozen revision: proved for classical groups by Lakshmibai, Musili and Seshadri (1979) via standard monomial theory, and extended to all reductive algebraic groups by Peter Littelmann in his 1998 paper 'Cones, crystals, and patterns' (Transformation Groups 3(2), 145-179) using the Littelmann path model. Nothing relevant happened in the 26 Jan 2024 - present window; the Wikipedia list entry is simply stale.
summary: The Demazure conjecture (1974) concerns whether certain Z-submodules of irreducible representations of algebraic groups are direct summands, i.e. whether Demazure's results on Schubert varieties extend from complex algebraic groups to algebraic groups over fields of other characteristics or over the integers. Both Wikipedia's own article on the conjecture and a corroborating Grokipedia summary state it was proved for classical groups (types A, B, C, D) by Lakshmibai-Musili-Seshadri in 1979 via standard monomial theory, and extended to all reductive algebraic groups by Littelmann in 1998 (identified via search as 'Cones, crystals, and patterns', Transform. Groups 3(2), 145-179) using the Littelmann path model. This is a fully digested, textbook-level result decades old, well before the 26 January 2024 window. I searched arXiv broadly for 'Demazure conjecture' activity in 2024-2025 and found only papers using the Demazure name for related but distinct combinatorial objects -- Demazure crystals, Demazure operators, Demazure products/atoms -- none of which are this conjecture (about integral structures / Z-submodule direct summands for algebraic group representations) restated or extended; they are different problems that happen to share the Demazure name (per the scope rule in §3.1, these are not cases or restatements of the stated conjecture). No AI system is involved anywhere in this history; the only credited work is by human mathematicians in 1979 and 1998. This is a clear case of the Wikipedia list retaining an already-solved problem, hence status open_stale rather than open or resolved (resolved would incorrectly imply resolution happened within or bears on the measurement window).
competing_reading: One could argue the correct status is simply 'resolved' rather than 'open_stale' on the grounds that the result is settled and expert-digested. However, per §6.1, open_stale is specifically for problems settled before the frozen revision's date and never counted as a change in the window, which is exactly this case -- the resolution predates the 26 Jan 2024 snapshot by 26-45 years, so open_stale is the correct code, not resolved (which would misleadingly suggest the resolution is part of what happened since 2024).
what_would_settle_it: Nothing further is needed to settle the classification; the only way this could change is if a source were found showing the 1979/1998 resolution was later found flawed or incomplete and reopened/refined within the 2024-2026 window, which no search here turned up.
